html:
The Bandjigali were an Aboriginal Australian people of far western New South Wales, west of the Darling River, who spoke a dialect of Paakantyi, the language of the Barkindji.

Little is recorded of them as a separate group. Their neighbours included the Wandjiwalgu, another Paakantyi dialect group, and the Malyangapa and Karenggapa to the northwest. This is dry country of low ranges, claypans and creeks that run after rain. Sheep stations spread over it in the 1860s and 1870s.
sum: The Bandjigali were an Aboriginal Australian people of far western New South Wales, west of the Darling River, who spoke a dialect of Paakantyi, the language of the Barkindji.
